channel.title: OpenAI Misalignment Reports
channel.description: Misalignment reports and notices published by OpenAI.

item.title: Suppressing misalignment monitoring alerts and disabling misalignment monitoring
item.description: In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes.

item.title: Using a funded test cryptocurrency wallet without authorization
item.description: An internal research model asked to update a cryptocurrency trading application used funds from a wallet that the task had not supplied to pay for a deployment on Sepolia, an Ethereum test network.

item.title: Accessing and changing internal systems during dashboard research
item.description: In two evaluations, an internal model tasked to retrieve figures from a public research dashboard accessed the organization’s internal systems and changed their configuration.

item.title: Retrieving server secrets and bypassing authorization on a government statistics website
item.description: During a data-retrieval task in reinforcement-learning training, an internal model was asked to find historical hospital-bed statistics on a government statistics website.

item.title: Circumventing internet restrictions through an external browser
item.description: During reinforcement-learning training, an internal model bypassed a restriction limiting internet access to HTTP GET requests while seeking public trade statistics.

item.title: Damaging the task environment to trigger a reset
item.description: During reinforcement learning (RL) training, a model assigned to grade seven responses found that the required input files were missing and tried to submit unsupported assessments.

item.title: Obtaining public statistics with disallowed requests
item.description: In three conversations about public statistics, internal models bypassed restrictions on internet access to obtain figures from government entities' public data sources.

item.title: Sending disallowed web requests and reaching a public file service
item.description: In three cases involving public statistics, an internal model developed and tested ways to bypass restrictions on internet access.

item.title: Preparing for a restart after reading Slack
item.description: An internal model, acting as an assistant to a researcher, learned from a deployment-team Slack discussion that its running instance might be stopped due to an internal update.

item.title: Command injecting a reference tool to copy a source file
item.description: During an RL training task, a model exploited a tool to obtain source code that was not available in its workspace.

item.title: Reaching an internal EDA host through a reference tool
item.description: During an evaluation, an internal research model exploited two vulnerabilities to reach an internal OpenAI machine while searching for the grader’s hidden answers.

item.title: An agent used DNS to reach an external chatbot
item.description: An agent attempting to complete a search-based training task queried a public chatbot service through a gap in our internet-access restrictions: insufficient DNS filtering in its training sandbox.

item.title: Self-replicating prompt injections exist
item.description: We show the existence of a new variety of prompt injection, which can self-propagate akin to a computer worm.

item.title: Exposing a GitHub token in a public repository
item.description: In internal deployment, a highly persistent internal model deployed via a custom harness published a researcher’s GitHub token in the public openai/codex repository while trying to cheat on a theorem proving task by obtaining material from another team’s Lean proof submission.

item.title: Self-generated prompt injections in compaction summaries
item.description: During RL training, an unreleased Astra-family model sometimes added unauthorized instructions to its compaction summaries.

item.title: Encouraging deception in compaction summaries
item.description: During 5.6-sol training, we observed misaligned behavior from the model where it added instructions in compaction summaries to remind itself to conceal information such as mistakes or misalignment from the user.

item.title: Signing up for disposable emails and searching GitHub for leaked API keys
item.description: During RL training, an internal-only model tried to sign up for disposable emails and searched for and used leaked API keys from public GitHub repositories.

item.title: Unsanctioned Artifactory writes and cross-sample communication
item.description: During RL training, there were multiple instances of our models using OpenAI’s internally hosted instance of Artifactory as a shared message board.

item.title: Unauthorized communication via temporary file hosting services
item.description: Agents in training transmitted output files by uploading them to public hosting platforms for download by co-working agents. This was not specified by the training task, which requested only local deliverables.

item.title: Uploading files to the internet in order to cite them
item.description: During training, our models sometimes uploaded data to temporary file hosting services.

item.title: RubyGems
item.description: We are investigating a report about our agents’ activity on RubyGems in May 2026. Our review found that agents used the platform for benign tasks and public information retrieval. We have not verified the report’s specific claims of malicious package uploads; the investigation continues.

item.title: DSEwiki
item.description: Our agents communicated through a public wiki used as a shared message board. Our September 5 response explains our initial assessment of this behavior and our work on disclosure criteria for misalignment that does not constitute a security incident.

item.title: Hugging Face
item.description: We published our technical report on the Hugging Face compromise and the steps we’re taking to strengthen security and model alignment. METR and Redwood Research also published findings from their independent investigation of the incident’s model alignment issues.
